title: Ph.D. Project ARIES: Efficient Mapping and Automated Compilation for AMD Versal Devices
problem: Heterogeneous architectures like AMD Versal ACAP devices present dual challenges: (1) achieving high-performance mapping solutions across diverse compute elements (CPUs, FPGAs, AIEs), and (2) providing programming abstractions that ensure high productivity, hindering adoption by non-hardware experts.
motivation: AI applications are increasingly memory and computation intensive, driving specialized AI chip development. AMD Versal ACAP devices offer promising heterogeneous solutions for continuous compute scaling, but complexity barriers limit their adoption beyond hardware specialists.
method: Systematic design space exploration for transformer-based workloads through mapping different layers to various system components (CPUs, FPGAs, AIEs) with latency-throughput trade-off analysis. Introduction of ARIES, an MLIR-based multi-level intermediate representation compilation framework providing unified IR for end-to-end AIE deployment.
key_novelty: Among the first to explore efficient heterogeneous mapping for Versal systems. ARIES is the first unified MLIR-based intermediate representation enabling end-to-end application deployment on AIE architectures, significantly enhancing programming productivity.
contributions: Comprehensive design space exploration for transformer workloads across heterogeneous Versal components
ARIES: multi-level MLIR-based compilation framework with unified IR
Analysis of latency-throughput trade-offs for heterogeneous mapping
Programming abstraction enabling non-specialists to leverage heterogeneous systems
Body of work published across FPGA'23, DAC'23, TRETS'24, FPGA'24, TCAD'24, with FPGA'25 Best Paper Nomination
hardware_target: AMD Versal ACAP devices (CPUs, FPGAs, AIEs)
baselines: Not explicitly specified; implicit comparison against prior heterogeneous mapping approaches
limitations: Not explicitly discussed in abstract; implicit: heterogeneous architecture complexity and design space exploration scope
primary_theme: Compiler and Automated Mapping for Heterogeneous AI Accelerators
